newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Vietnam diamond drill successful-Spectrum.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam diamond drill successful-Spectrum.

text.p: Spectrum Resources Ltd said on Thursday its diamond drilling program at the Ban Phuc Nickel Project in Vietnam had been successfully completed.
"The drilling programme has been very successful with 1,220 metres completed in eleven holes," the company said in a statement.
Ban Phuc is a mineralised magmatic nickel copper system consisting of a massive sulphide deposit peripheral to an olivine rich intrusion.

The intrusion itself also contains magmatic segregations of nickel sulphides. Previous drilling in 1959 to 1963 within the massive sulphide zone had outlined an indicated resource of 985,000 tonnes grading 3.55 percent nickel and 1.30 percent copper.

"The purpose of the 1996 drill programme was to establish continuity of mineralisation within the previously identified massive sulphide ore body and to further investigate Ni-Cu mineralisation within the intrusive," Spectrum said.
"The drilling has established that mineralisation in the shear hosted massive sulphides is continuous and of high grade over the upper levels."
Individual samples assayed up to 7.49 percent nickel, 2.36 percent copper and 0.16 percent cobalt over 1.3 metres.

Spectrum said the results confirmed the reliability of the data collected by Vietnamese drilling in 1959-1963. It also provided valuable geological information that may direct further drilling towards additional resources, the company said.

Spectrum said no information was yet available on the detailed geology of drill hole LK 46, but if the nickel-mineralised zones found in LK 46 could be correlated with those in nearby hole BP 96-7, a significant increase in resources at Ban Phuc was probable.
Spectrum said further drilling will commence at Ban Phuc in the near future.
Drilling is underway on the Na Ka prospect, 25 kilometres west of Ban Phuc.
Spectrum, through its subsidiary Asian Mineral Resources Ltd, has a 70 percent interest in the Ta Khoa licence of 600 square kilometres which contains Ban Phuc.
